statement: Cones and cylinders which are on equal bases are to one another as their heights.
heath_proof: For let EB, FD be cylinders on equal bases, the circles AB, CD; I say that, as the cylinder EB is to the cylinder FD, so is the axis GH to the axis KL. For let the axis KL be produced to the point N, let LN be made equal to the axis GH, and let the cylinder CM be conceived about LN as axis. Since then the cylinders EB, CM are of the same height, they are to one another as their bases. [XII. 11] But the bases are equal to one another; therefore the cylinders EB, CM are also equal. And, since the cylinder FM has been cut by the plane CD which is parallel to its opposite planes, therefore, as the cylinder CM is to the cylinder FD, so is the axis LN to the axis KL. [XII. 13] But the cylinder CM is equal to the cylinder EB, and the axis LN to the axis GH; therefore, as the cylinder EB is to the cylinder FD, so is the axis GH to the axis KL. But, as the cylinder EB is to the cylinder FD, so is the cone ABG to the cone CDK. [XII. 10] Therefore also, as the axis GH is to the axis KL, so is the cone ABG to the cone CDK and the cylinder EB to the cylinder FD.
ai_proof_text:
12.14
**Statement:** Cones and cylinders which are on equal bases are to one another as their heights.

**Step 1.** Let AB and CD be equal circles with centres H and L. Let EB be the cylinder on the base AB with axis GH, described by the rectangle GHBE (right-angled at H) carried round the fixed side GH, and let FD be the cylinder on the base CD with axis KL, described by the rectangle KLDF carried round KL; thus HB and LD are radii of the bases AB, CD, and KF is a radius of the opposite base of FD (D11.21, D11.22, D11.23). Let ABG and CDK be the cones on the same bases AB, CD described by the right-angled triangles GHB, KLD carried round the same sides GH, KL, so that their vertices are G, K and their axes are GH, KL (D11.18, D11.19, D11.20).

**Step 2.** The height of each of these solids is its axis. For GH makes a right angle with HB in every position which HB takes as it is carried round; hence GH makes right angles with every straight line in the plane of the circle AB which meets it, and so is at right angles to that plane (D11.3). Therefore the perpendicular from G to the base AB is GH itself, that is, the height of the cylinder EB and of the cone ABG is GH (D6.4); in the same way the height of the cylinder FD and of the cone CDK is KL. It is therefore required to prove that cylinder EB : cylinder FD = GH : KL and cone ABG : cone CDK = GH : KL.

**Step 3.** Produce KL beyond L to N (P2) and cut off LN equal to GH (1.3). Produce FD beyond D to M (P2), cut off DM equal to LN (1.3), and join NM (P1).

**Step 4.** The angles KLD, LDF are right, being angles of the rectangle KLDF; hence the adjacent angles NLD, LDM are also right (1.13). The straight line LD falling on KN and FM thus makes the interior angles NLD, LDM on the same side equal to two right angles, so that LN is parallel to DM (1.28); and LN is equal to DM. Therefore NM, which joins their extremities in the same directions, is equal and parallel to LD (1.33), and LNMD is a parallelogram. Its angles at L and D being right, the opposite angles at M and N are also right (1.34); so LNMD is a rectangle with sides LN, LD. Further, KF and NM are each at right angles to KN, so that KF is parallel to NM (1.28), and KN is parallel to FM, as shown; hence KNMF, whose four angles are right, is a rectangle, made up of the rectangles KLDF and LNMD lying on opposite sides of LD.

**Step 5.** Let the rectangle KNMF be carried round the fixed side KN and restored to the position from which it began to move. It describes a cylinder FM, whose axis is KN and whose bases are the circles described by KF and NM (D11.21, D11.22, D11.23). In this same revolution the part KLDF describes the given cylinder FD, and the part LNMD describes a cylinder CM whose axis is LN and whose base is the circle described by LD, namely the circle CD (D11.21, D11.22, D11.23). Thus the cylinder FM is made up of the two cylinders FD and CM, which lie on opposite sides of the plane of the circle CD.

**Step 6.** The straight line KN makes right angles with KF, LD and NM in every position which they take as they are carried round; hence it is at right angles to the plane of each of the three circles described by them (D11.3), and these three planes are parallel to one another (11.14). Therefore the cylinder FM is cut by the plane of the circle CD, which is parallel to its opposite planes, into the cylinders CM and FD, whose axes are LN and LK; consequently, as the cylinder CM is to the cylinder FD, so is the axis LN to the axis LK (12.13).

**Step 7.** The cylinders EB and CM are of the same height, for their heights are their axes GH and LN (Step 2), and LN was made equal to GH. Therefore, as the cylinder EB is to the cylinder CM, so is the base AB to the base CD (12.11). But the base AB is equal to the base CD. In this proportion take of the first and third the magnitudes themselves, the cylinder EB and the circle AB, and of the second and fourth the cylinder CM and the circle CD, each taken once, which is a case of equimultiples: since the circle AB neither exceeds nor falls short of the circle CD but is equal to it, the cylinder EB likewise neither exceeds nor falls short of the cylinder CM but is equal to it (D5.5). Therefore the cylinder EB is equal to the cylinder CM.

**Step 8.** Since the cylinder EB is equal to the cylinder CM, the two have the same ratio to the cylinder FD (5.7): EB : FD = CM : FD. Since GH is equal to LN, likewise GH : LK = LN : LK (5.7). But CM : FD = LN : LK (Step 6). Therefore, ratios which are the same with the same ratio being the same with one another (5.11), cylinder EB : cylinder FD = GH : KL.

**Step 9.** The cone ABG has the same base AB and the same height GH as the cylinder EB; therefore it is a third part of the cylinder EB, that is, the cylinder EB is triple the cone ABG (12.10). In the same way the cylinder FD is triple the cone CDK. Thus the cones ABG, CDK are the same parts (thirds) of the cylinders EB, FD, and parts have the same ratio as the same multiples of them taken in corresponding order (5.15); hence cone ABG : cone CDK = cylinder EB : cylinder FD. But cylinder EB : cylinder FD = GH : KL (Step 8); therefore cone ABG : cone CDK = GH : KL (5.11).

**Step 10.** Therefore the cylinders EB, FD on the equal bases AB, CD are to one another as their heights GH, KL, and so also are the cones ABG, CDK on the same bases. Q.E.D.
